$comment: The disk tile cache's KEY LAYOUT and HIT RULE, as one table read by both
The duplication is deliberate — the CLI and the API are meant to share one cache
directory, and neither language can call the other — but 'deliberate' only holds
while the two agree. What they have to agree about is not the code; it is these
1. layout      where a tile is written, relative to the cache root.
2. hitNames    which filenames in {source}/{z}/{x} count as a finished tile for
{y}. Both sides document the same trap: a plain '{y}.*' glob also
matches the '{y}.{ext}.tmp-…' file each writes before its rename,
so a concurrent reader would be served a half-written tile as a
hit and the atomic rename would be for nothing.
3. escaping    keys that resolve outside the root. Both treat these as a miss on
read and skip the write, rather than writing where they were told.
Companion to tile-content-types.json, which pins the extension mapping. Between
them, a tile written by either side is found and served correctly by the other.
Change a rule here and BOTH suites fail, which is the point.

hitNames.why: extensionless, written before the ext was recorded

hitNames.name: 6202.png.tmp-4821-1757600000000
hitNames.why: the half-written temp file; a '{y}.*' glob matches it and would serve a torn tile

hitNames.name: 6202.tmp-4821
hitNames.why: same trap without an extension in the name

hitNames.name: 62020.png
hitNames.why: a different tile whose stem starts the same

hitNames.name: 0.png
hitNames.why: y=0 is a real tile, not a falsy one
